description.narrative: The development objective of the Metro Colombo Urban Development Project for Sri Lanka is to support the Borrower to (i) reduce flooding in the catchment of the Colombo Water Basin, and (ii) strengthen the capacity of local authorities in the Colombo Metropolitan Area (CMA) to rehabilitate, improve and maintain local infrastructure and services through selected demonstration investments. There are three components to the project. The first component of the project is flood and drainage management. This supports priority improvements to flood and drainage management infrastructure in the Colombo Water Basin, development of an integrated flood management system (IFMS), and complementary interventions to improve environment and public facilities along the water bodies. The second component of the project is urban development, infrastructure rehabilitation and capacity building for Metro Colombo local authorities. This component aims to strengthen strategic planning processes at the metropolitan level, and support local authorities in the Colombo Metropolitan Area to rehabilitate and manage streets and drainage infrastructure, and improve local public facilities and other urban services. The third component of the project is implementation support. This component provides support to implementation agencies in areas such as project management, monitoring and evaluation (M&E), procurement, financial management, and environmental and social safeguards; construction supervision; communications and public awareness; and operating costs and equipments needed by the Project Management Unit (PMU), Project Implementation Agencies and Project Local Authorities.

The project development objective (PDO) is to support the Borrower to (i) reduce flooding in the catchment of the Colombo WaterBasin, and (ii) strengthen the capacity of local authorities in the Colombo Metropolitan Area (CMA) to rehabilitate, improve andmaintainlocal infrastructure and services through selected demonstration investments.

title.narrative: 1.1 Length of primary canals improved by the project

comment.narrative: <p>All interventions for improved primary canals were fully completed and exceeded the indicator target. </p>

title.narrative: Reduction in the area under risk of flooding (50-year return period) in the project area.

comment.narrative: <p>On June 10, 2016, the Project Management Unit provided an update of the impact on the PDO if Madiwela Diversion is notcompleted. The end target was revised as part of the restructuring in 2017. The revised end target was based on technical analysis to better align with the indicator and likelihood to achieve the target by project closing date. </p>

title.narrative: 1.4 Micro-drainage subprojects implemented under the Project that reduce risk of flooding in localised areas (10 year return period)

comment.narrative: <p>At appraisal, 15 micro drainage was proposed by the municipal council. At implementation, the project focused on 6 micro drainage improvements based on their feasibility. At closure, the project completed 5 and partially completed Norris Canal diversion. </p>

title.narrative: 2.2 Km of road/drainage built/rehabilitated based on prescribed standards

comment.narrative: <p>Major road around Colombo Metro Area were rehabilitated. In total, 47 km road rehabilitated including sidewalks. This exceeded the target and all were completed within the first 4 years of project implementation. </p>
<p>Drainage capacity was improved following completion of macro-drainage interventions and it exceeded the target.</p>

title.narrative: 1.3 Increase in drainage capacity (pumping system, subject to the results of the hydrological model)

comment.narrative: <p>Fully achieved by completion of North Lock pumping station, St. Sebastian South, and Ambatale pumping station. The total capacity of these 3 pumping stations are 60 m3.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of total urban roads maintained by PLAs that are in good and fair condition in the 4 PLAs
3.1 RTC developed and integrated into SLLRDC's operation

comment.narrative: <p>Real Time Center developed under the project, located in a building constructed using GOSL funds under the project. The IFMS is housed in this building and managed by SLLDC and integrated to its system. </p>

title.narrative: 2.8 Public convenience complexes maintained by PLAs that are in good and fair condition.

comment.narrative: <p>16 public toilets around Colombo, including within public parks and wetland parks were improved and maintained by the municipal council. </p>

title.narrative: 2.7 Number of public spaces / parks upgraded and revitalized by the project

comment.narrative: <p>3 major public parks in the heart of Colombo were successfully improved and maintained by the municipal council and the urban development authority. </p>

title.narrative: 2.6 Users satisfied with area-based demonstration projects in Colombo City

comment.narrative: <p>Direct beneficiaries indicated satisfaction of improved public parks including Linear Park, Townhall area, and Viharamadevi Park. </p>

title.narrative: 1.6 Users satisfaction with the condition of Beira Lake and Beddagana and Rampart Park

comment.narrative: <p>Beneficiary satisfaction survey was conducted for Beddagana Wetland Park, Viharamadevi Park, and Kotte Rampart. Respondents were direct beneficiaries, of which 83 percent were satisfied with the completed interventions under the project. </p>
